Rashi on Menachot 21b:13:1.english: No, it is needed - For the court to stipulate that the priests may salt their offerings from [salt] of the Temple treasury.

Rashi on Menachot 21b:13:2.english: Only according to ben Bukhri - Who says that priests are not obligated in shekels.

Rashi on Menachot 21b:14:1.english: Any priest who pays the shekel - Who brings his shekel to the Chamber in Adar.

Rashi on Menachot 21b:14:2.hebrew: אינו חוטא - מדקאמר אינו חוטא, מכלל דלכתחילה לא מיחייב. וטעמא מפרש במס' שקלים, דכתיב: כל העובר על הפקודים, ושבט לוי לא נפקד. ואע"ג דאיכא למימר: הא מייתי חולין לעזרה, אפילו הכי אינו חוטא, כדמפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Menachot 21b:14:2.english: He is not a sinner - From [the fact] that he says "he is not a sinner," by implication, ab initio he is not obligated [to contribute]. And the reason is explained in Tractate Shekalim: As it is written: "Everyone who passes among those who are numbered" (Exodus 30:13), and the tribe of Levi was not numbered. And even though there is room to say: "Behold, he is bringing non-sacred items into the [Temple] courtyard," even so, he is not a sinner, as [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Menachot 21b:14:3.hebrew: כל כהן שאינו שוקל חוטא - בשקלים מפרש טעמא, דכתיב: זה יתנו - זה בגימטריא שנים עשר שבטים, והיינו שבט לוי. וכל העובר, מפרש התם: כל העובר בים סוף:
Rashi on Menachot 21b:14:3.english: Any priest who does not pay the shekel is a sinner - In [Tractate] Shekalim, the reason is explained: As it is written: "This they shall give" (Exodus 30:13) — "this" [zeh] in gematria is twelve, [corresponding to the] twelve tribes, and that includes the tribe of Levi. And "everyone who passes," it explains there [means]: Everyone who crossed the Red Sea.

Rashi on Menachot 21b:14:4.hebrew: לעצמן - להנאתן, וקא פריך: ולבן בוכרי כו':
Rashi on Menachot 21b:14:4.english: For themselves - For their own benefit, and [the Gemara] asks: "And according to ben Bukhri, etc."

Rashi on Menachot 21b:17:1.english: It might enter your mind to say, etc. - And now [the Gemara] explains the "it was only necessary" [stated] above.

Tosafot on Menachot 21b:14:1.hebrew: כל כהן ששוקל אינו חוטא - לבן בוכרי, אפילו לוים פטורים כמו כהנים, כדפריש טעמא במסכת שקלים: כל העובר על הפקודים, ושבט לוי לא נפקד. אבל רבן יוחנן בן זכאי דריש: כל העובר – עובר בים סוף. אף על גב דכתיב בפרשת אלה פקודי מאת ככר ואלף ותשעה, היינו לתרומת האדנים, דשלש תרומות היו, כדמפרש בקונטרס בפרשת כי תשא; ובאותה של האדנים לא היה שבט לוי, אבל באותה של צורך קרבנות היו. והשתא ניחא טפי: הא דכתיב כל העובר, בים סוף [משמע], (על הפקודים דהא) [והא] דכתיב על הפקודים – משום תרומת אדנים. ומיהו, בלא"ה יש לפרש: כל העובר על הפקודים – שנפקדו, בין לבדם בין עם ישראל:
Tosafot on Menachot 21b:14:1.english: Any priest who contributes the shekel is not a sinner - According to ben Bukhri, even Levites are exempt, just like priests, as the reason is explained in tractate Shekalim: [The verse states,] "Whoever passes among those numbered" (Exodus 30:13), and the tribe of Levi was not numbered [in that census]. But Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai expounds: "Whoever passes" [means] whoever passed through the Red Sea. Even though it is written in Parashat Elleh Pekudei, "a hundred talents and a thousand and nine" [i.e., 1,775 shekels; Exodus 38:25], that was for the contribution of the sockets (adanim), for there were three contributions, as explained in the Kuntres [by Rashi] in Parashat Ki Tisa; and in that [contribution] of the sockets the tribe of Levi was not [included], but in that [contribution] for the needs of the offerings, they were [included]. And now, [the verse] is understood much better: That which is written, "Whoever passes," implies [those who passed] through the Red Sea; and that which is written, "among those numbered," is because of the contribution of the sockets. However, even without this [distinction], it can be explained: "Whoever passes among those numbered" [includes all] who were numbered, whether by themselves or with [the rest of] Israel.

Tosafot on Menachot 21b:14:2.hebrew: שהכהנים דורשין מקרא זה לעצמן - משמע דרבן יוחנן בן זכאי לא היה כהן. והא דתניא בסיפרי גבי פרה, שאמר רבן יוחנן בן זכאי לתלמידיו מה שעשו ושרתו ידי שכחתי — לאו דהוא עצמו קאמר, אלא כלומר: ע"פ הוראתו. והא דמסקינן התם: ויש אומרים הילל היה, אלא שלא היה יכול לומר מה שעשו ושרתו ידי — היינו טעמא, לפי שלא שרפו פרה בימיו:
Tosafot on Menachot 21b:14:2.english: That the priests expound this verse for themselves - This implies that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was not a priest. And that which is taught in the Sifrei regarding the [red] heifer, that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to his disciples, "What my hands have done and ministered I have forgotten" — [this does] not [mean] that he himself [performed the service], but rather, as if to say, according to his instruction. And that which is concluded there, "And some say it was Hillel, but he was not able to say: What my hands have done and ministered" — the reason is that they did not burn a [red] heifer in his days.
